validated_results.title: Circulating fatty acids and prostate cancer risk: individual participant meta-analysis of prospective studies.
authors: Endogenous Hormones, Nutritional Biomarkers and Prostate Cancer Collaborative Group
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Pooled analysis of individual participant data from seven prospective studies reporting circulating eicosapentaenoic acid and incident prostate cancer risk, providing an original target-specific estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest study-specific fifth (Q5 vs Q1)
extraction.timing: prospective pre-diagnostic blood measurement, average follow-up 5.1 years
extraction.population: prostate cancer case patients and control patients from seven prospective studies

effect_size.excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was, respectively, 14% and 16% greater in the highest fifth of eicosapentaenoic acid (20:5n-3) (OR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.01 to 1.29, Ptrend = .001) and docosapentaenoic acid (22:5n-3) (OR = 1.16, 95% CI = 1.02 to 1.33, P trend = .003), but in each case there was heterogeneity between studies (P = .022 and P < .001, respectively).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was, respectively, 14% and 16% greater in the highest fifth of eicosapentaenoic acid (20:5n-3) (OR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.01 to 1.29, Ptrend = .001) and docosapentaenoic acid (22:5n-3) (OR = 1.16, 95% CI = 1.02 to 1.33, P trend = .003), but in each case there was heterogeneity between studies (P = .022 and P < .001, respectively).

comparison.excerpt: Prostate cancer risk by study-specific fifths of 14 fatty acids

design.excerpt: estimated using multivariable-adjusted conditional logistic regression

timing.excerpt: with an average follow-up of 5.1 (SD = 3.3) years

exposure_measurement.excerpt: individual participant data on circulating fatty acids (weight percent)
